title: Barclays lifts S&P 500 year-end target to 7,950 after standout tech earnings season - TradingView
text: Barclays lifts S&P 500 year-end target to 7,950 after standout tech earnings season Less than 1 min read SPX Barclays raised its year-end S&P 500 ( SP500 ) target to 7,950 from 7,800 on Wednesday, arguing that a technology-led earnings season has strengthened the case for durable, AI-supported profit growth. Head of U.S. equity strategy Venu Krishna said recent results point to “standout” tech execution and greater visibility on AI-driven earnings, even as a more hawkish rate outlook keeps the firm conservative on valuations. Barclays also lifted its 2026 S&P 500 earnings-per-share forecast to $365 from $337 and reiterated an 8,800 year-end 2027 index target. The new 2026 mark sits about 3.6% above Tuesday’s close of 7,673.52. The financial institution said continued AI investment and solid economic activity should sustain earnings momentum in coming quarters. It remains cautious, however, citing questions about the durability of AI spending, sticky inflation, geopolitical risk, and limited room for multiple expansion. Currently the S&P 500 is up just under 12% year to date. The Barclays upgrade follows HSBC’s Tuesday move, which lifted its year-end 2026 target to 8,100 from 7,650 on similar earnings and AI-infrastructure arguments. Together, the revisions underscore a Wall Street tilt toward profit-led gains rather than a broad valuation rerating.
